topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by relating the material to previous histopathology practicals and setting out the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental methods for assaying cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the main categories of cancer-associated mutations and illustrate their functional effects and dosage genetics using key regulators such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinctions between sequence and chromosome instability and detail the specific repair, replication, and mitotic defects that cause them.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancers evolve through the sequential accumulation of mutations and how inherited germline defects accelerate this multi-step development.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session by confirming that learning outcomes were met, suggesting supplementary reading, and previewing the upcoming lecture.
